▶ 75.1% of the time inside instrumented I/O library calls is library code rather than syscalls (22.189 thread-seconds cumulative across 25 threads, 0.888 s per thread in a 3.850 s run), led by
H5F__close_cb:0x1562b0 at 20.1%
↪ cumulative across 25 thread(s) in a 3.850 s run: 29.536 thread-seconds inside instrumented library calls, of which 7.547 s is syscalls and 22.189 s is library code (75.1%)
↪ that is 0.888 s of library code per thread on average, against a 3.850 s wall-clock span
↪ 103 distinct instrumented function(s) appear in the trace -- where internal helpers are traced as well as the API boundary, most library time is expected to sit above the syscall layer
↪ exclusive (self) time by function, so a caller is not charged for what it calls:
↪ H5F__close_cb:0x1562b0: 4.458 s self (20.1% of library code)
↪ H5FL_reg_malloc:0x1a5980: 3.458 s self (15.6% of library code)
↪ H5F__create_api_common:0x1486b0: 3.075 s self (13.9% of library code)
↪ MPI_Finalize:0x778a0: 2.493 s self (11.2% of library code)
↪ MPI_Init_thread:0x80d20: 2.295 s self (10.3% of library code)
↪ H5FL_reg_calloc:0x1a5b00: 1.880 s self (8.5% of library code)
Recommendations:
↪ The largest single consumer of library time is H5F__close_cb:0x1562b0 (20.1% of it, 4.458 s cumulative) -- look there first rather than at the storage configuration
↪ Several of the top consumers are HDF5 free-list and memory management routines, which points at object churn rather than I/O: reuse dataspace, datatype and property-list identifiers
instead of creating and closing them per access, and consider raising the chunk cache so chunks are not repeatedly allocated and evicted
